reasons.A1: Select one bounded falsifier investment. Algorithm-family changes plus genuine derived-state maintenance could distribute a partial rule edit across necessary update and observation relations. This is a concrete comprehension/edit hypothesis, with no established obstacle to clean functional replacement. It merits testing only against existing APIs and the cheapest independent reimplementation lanes.
reasons.A2: Do not select. No concrete existing noncryptographic kernel/edit survived the clean circuit extraction and projection-patching challenge. Runtime and source expansion could account for the entire apparent attacker cost. Word-level reconstruction is not necessary for every useful explanation, edit or replacement.
reasons.A3: Do not select separately. Quotienting future-equivalent states can simplify the attacker's machine. History count does not establish complexity or resistance; useful residualization may support A1 without consuming another architecture slot.

requiredConditions: Freeze three existing evaluator roots, authored event/observation APIs and partial edit tickets before choosing implementations or inspecting attack results. Report rejected roots and easy controls without replacing them with favorable synthetic tasks.

Numeric domains, bounds, duplicate multiplicities, ordering, deletion behavior, exceptions and observable identities must follow authored semantics. Preserve required base records and key-to-record information; never change the API to justify removing them.

Every alternative must be a genuinely applicable algorithm family with exact initialization, reset, updates and observations. One ordinary JavaScript realization is emitted; no server, secret, generic VM fallback or second easy direct implementation is introduced.

Give ordinary and transformed implementations identical public schema, task information and resources. Audit whether the edit ticket itself supplies a full replacement specification, but do not withhold legitimately public information to obstruct rebuilding.

Permit added attacker state, event replay, omission or synthesis of events, output patches, clean machine extraction and complete shadow reimplementation. Requiring an in-place edit of the protected artifact is prohibited.

Score correct partial edits and checkable comprehension separately using hidden unchanged behaviors and future histories, including cold start, reset, deletion, duplicates and numeric boundaries. Do not require attribution of a non-identifiable original algorithm or source names.
Keep functional replacement, unchanged artifact reuse, cosmetic reprinting and meaningful clean-machine extraction distinct. Disclose cheap cloning even if edit or comprehension tasks prove harder.

Measure minimum successful attacker cost, setup/transfer and all legitimate runtime, cold-start, memory, output-size and compile costs. Stop when a reusable sidecar, replay strategy or extractor solves the actual tasks at comparable cost; surviving the pilot is not a security multiplier or product approval.
cheapestDefeat: Observe the full public event stream, reconstruct original tuples in attacker-added state, and implement the amended rule from the public schema and edit ticket while preserving unspecified outputs using the available artifact or a clean extracted machine. This can avoid learning the maintained-view invariants entirely. Separately, lifting initialization, updates and projections into a usable state machine can defeat cloning claims without reconstructing owner algorithms.
firstExperiment: On three frozen existing synchronous evaluator roots, produce three applicable algorithm-family realizations under the same exact API and cost envelope. First run a clean transition extractor and ticket-driven shadow evaluator with reset/replay; then attempt partial join, predicate or multiplicity edits plus invariant/consequence explanations on held-out histories. Include ordinary optimized code and actually functional eligible historical baselines on their protected intersection. If comparable-cost attacks succeed, stop A1 rather than adding masking or more state. Only a survivor justifies a larger preregistered study.
